ingredientGroups.heading: The classic build-ins (choose to the table)

ingredients.item: /2 cucumber, deseeded and small-diced — the cold-noodle classic's version
Thin slivers of Asian pear for the raw-seafood lane

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Vinegar, honey, and water whisked clear; gochujang in, worked to one even red-orange with no dark streaks.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a spoon dragged through leaves a slowly-closing trail — the thickness of thick honey for the noodle build.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Garlic, sesame oil, sesame seeds; the build-ins to the bowl's job; a final taste — the vinegar should be present on the finish of a dipped finger, a clean snap after the sweet.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test on a piece of plain cucumber: snap, sweet, heat hum, acid line. If the cucumber tastes pickled in ten seconds of sitting, the vinegar ran a splash heavy; if it reads as plain gochujang, the vinegar is shy.

visualDonenessCues: a spoon dragged through leaves a slowly-closing trail — the thickness of thick honey for the noodle build.

the eating test on a piece of plain cucumber: snap, sweet, heat hum, acid line. If the cucumber tastes pickled in ten seconds of sitting, the vinegar ran a splash heavy; if it reads as plain gochujang, the vinegar is shy.
storageNotes: Keeps 1 week refrigerated and genuinely improves on days two and three as the vinegar mellows into the paste. Cucumber build-ins go in at serving, not storage.

Variations: the raw-seafood build with pear slivers; a spoon over the jjukkumi record (#SF06) instead of the marinade for a lighter tent; thinned further with water and a drop of soy, it dresses the cold noodle bowls and the squid's leftovers.
